name: RelayDesk
adaptations: Python-only stratum (protocol permits it): the browser UI becomes server-rendered HTML pages at documented paths (/, /tickets/{id}, /login). Hidden tests only check that those pages return 200 HTML containing the relevant data; behaviour is asserted through the JSON API each request documents. Fonts are static assets at documented URLs.

Every request keeps the spec title and user prompt verbatim and adds a '## What I need' public contract (endpoints, JSON shapes, status/error codes, env vars, clock control and full fixture documentation for services introduced at that step). Spec evaluator check text, mutations and probes are not shown to agents.

All fictional services are one in-process threaded hub (hub.py) behind RELAYDESK_EXTERNAL_URL with per-service path prefixes (/pollen, /comet, /knowledge, /orders, /harbor, /quartz, /nimbus). Credentials are fixed test tokens published in the request that introduces each service; the hub records every call (including unknown routes) and supports scripted errors, Retry-After, holds, cut-off streams and Harbor poll counts.

The seed README carries the protocol's common technical envelope verbatim and the ci.json selector contract (from ChronoWeave request 5 in substance); the seed ci.json always prints ALL, stated as a valid starting point. ci_from_step is 3 (once real reply services exist).

Request 0: upload is a raw-body POST /api/imports (multipart parsing would need python-multipart, which is not in the locked environment). 'Cannot be read' is defined exactly (not UTF-8, empty, wrong header, wrong field count, empty field, invalid id, repeated id); ids already present are skipped and reported. The attached CSV is three synthetic tickets with non-ASCII text and a multi-line quoted body.
Request 1: 'show it again later' = reopen, with a status filter on the list (open by default, closed, all); search is a case-insensitive substring match on subject or customer email.

Request 2: connection details are set per service with PUT /api/connections/{service} {"token"}; accepting replaces the draft text (no merge mode); failures are recorded suggestions with codes provider_auth_failed / provider_error.
Request 3: the usual choice is GET/PUT /api/preferences (default pollen until changed); naming a provider in a request does not change it; GET /api/providers lists services available for new work.

Request 4: the 'simple test sign-in' is a RELAYDESK_TEAMS_FILE JSON (two teams, three users with passwords) with cookie sessions from POST /api/login; every /api/ endpoint except health and login needs a session (401 unauthenticated); another team's data answers 404 not_found; ticket ids are unique per team only; sessions may end at restart. Earlier-step hidden tests sign in from DRIFT_STEP 4.

Request 5: suggestions become asynchronous (202 + polling GET /api/suggestions/{id}); 'chunks visible before completion' is asserted as partial text while the hub holds the stream; providers gain a streaming flag. Earlier-step tests accept 202 and look for /pollen/draft/stream from DRIFT_STEP 5.

Request 6: the article service authenticates with a per-team bearer token plus a team query parameter (403 on mismatch); selected articles are fetched by id when asking; unknown ids are 422 unknown_article; sources are kept on suggestions and on the draft.

Request 7: lookups are saved on the ticket; dollars are formatted $1,234.56; order_ids must already be looked up on that ticket (422 unknown_order); asking for a suggestion never calls the order service.

Request 8: 'virtual time' is RELAYDESK_TIME_SCALE (real seconds per second of waiting; hidden tests use 0.05 and check each wait's lower bound and that it is not real seconds); only 429/503 are retried, 503 without Retry-After waits 1 second, exhaustion is provider_unavailable, a stream cut off after it started is not retried.

Request 9: Harbor uses a bearer token (the spec names no credential); poll at most once per second with the first poll at least one second after submission; a Harbor-side cancellation is provider_error.

Request 10: background work runs inside the process started from run.json (no separate worker command); 'restart halfway' is SIGKILL then start on the same data; suggestions gain a queued status; a submitted Harbor job must be resumed by job id (resubmission is a failure) while resending Pollen/Comet is permitted; 'no duplicate accepted draft' is checked as exactly one suggestion per batch item.

Request 11: POST /api/suggestions/{id}/cancel; Harbor gets one DELETE and polling stops; a cancelled suggestion never changes. Cancel-before-dispatch is checked opportunistically (an item observed queued right before cancelling must never reach the provider) because dispatch concurrency is the agent's choice.

Request 12: Quartz uses a bearer token; citations are {article_id,title,url} on every suggestion ([] for other services); 'no job polling or order-tool execution' is checked as only POST /responses and no order-service call when asking.

Request 13: codes provider_retired and choose_provider and a needs_choice preference field. Old Comet records are checked by an upgrade test that runs the candidate's own code from just before request 13 and then the current code on the same data. From DRIFT_STEP 13, earlier tests that needed a second non-streaming service use Harbor and Comet-specific checks become provider_retired checks.

Request 14: the two fonts are small synthetic WOFF2 files supplied base64 in the request and served at /static/fonts/*.woff2; 'remember in this browser' is a relaydesk_font cookie reflected as <body data-font>; no real browser font-loading check. 'Put live while jobs carry on' is an upgrade test from the pre-request-14 commit with a running Harbor job and a held Pollen batch item.

Request 15: orders v2 at /orders/v2/orders/{id}; the hub answers 410 on v1 from DRIFT_STEP 15; order objects replace total_cents with money and a formatted total ($, EUR, JPY rules). 'Mixed old/new deployment versions' is reduced to a stop/kill-and-start upgrade from the pre-request-15 commit (old dollar records plus a waiting reply).

Upgrade tests extract `git archive` of the commit that added docs/requests/<request>.md (the runner commits each request before the agent works) and run it with the candidate's .venv on a shared data directory; they need the candidate's git history, and a trajectory whose previous-step code cannot start fails them.

Not implemented in hidden tests (version 1): release rehearsal, built-artifact counts and hashes, independent frontend/backend/worker deployment, 'core edits for new integrations', selector mutation challenges and timing measures; the harness may measure some of these separately.

Sealed probes became concrete requests: p1 Nimbus (familiar streaming and retries; changed: X-Nimbus-Key header, instructions/context body, chunk/start/end events and a remote cancel endpoint); p2 inbox header #0B7A75 with 24px padding (artifact-hash comparison not implemented); p3 Quartz text_delta renamed output_text with both names accepted during switch-over, saved Quartz suggestions checked by upgrade; p4 order API v3 with decimal-string amounts and GBP, v2 retired (410), saved orders, drafts and a waiting reply checked by upgrade.
